title: Zero-shot request
change: One sentence: "Extract the details from this invoice." This is how most people start.
watch: The model decides which fields matter and how to format them. Dates and amounts come back exactly as printed, in local formats, so software can't use them.

title: Role and explicit task
change: Adds an accounts-payable role, names the exact fields, and asks for ISO dates, ISO currency codes and plain numbers.
watch: Values become more consistent, but the output is still prose. A human can read it; a payment system can't.

title: Output contract
change: Replaces the field list with a strict JSON shape, types, and null when a value is absent.
watch: The jump in machine-readability. Then look at what is still wrong: line-item counts and locale-dependent dates such as 05/03/2026 in Australia.

title: Show, don't only tell
change: Adds two worked examples (France and the USA). They demonstrate conventions that are awkward to describe, such as not counting shipping as a line item.
watch: Line-item counts and formats line up with the examples, without adding a single new rule.

title: Think before answering
change: Adds a "working" field the model fills first: identify the country's conventions, interpret dates and numbers, count lines, and do the arithmetic.
watch: Ambiguous dates and the UK invoice whose total doesn't add up. Reasoning also gives auditors a trail.

title: Guardrails
change: Wraps the invoice in tags, declares it untrusted, forbids inventing or correcting values, and adds an anomalies list.
watch: The Helix invoice hides instructions to set the total to zero. This step resists them and reports them as an anomaly.
